dct_description_sm: The Beaufort Sea provides marine and coastal habitat for hundreds of thousands of migrating, breeding, and moulting birds such as eiders, scoters, long-tailed ducks, scaup, and red-throated loons. Those species have declined in the last decades, though it is important to assess the potential impacts from oil and gas activities (disturbance and habitat loss, attraction to offshore platforms and rigs, and risk of accidental spills and chronic discharge of pollutants) on birds in the Beaufort Sea. The aim of this project is to evaluate the coastal and nearshore bird usage of the Canadian Beaufort Sea. This will help developers and regulators develop mitigation measures to reduce impacts on birds, facilitate environmental assessment process for oil and gas development, and ensure that important bird areas are known and receive priority protection in the event of a spill. This project will conclude in products such as Geospatial database with coastal and nearshore bird data, hard-copy report with updated information on species numbers, and distributions of birds in Beaufort Region at specific times of the year, online mapping system that outlines important bird areas and prioritized list of future bird survey needs.
dct_title_s: Coastal and Marine Bird Usage of the Beaufort Sea
